## VSiN on this hire — The Coaching Carousel Never Stops

*Adam Burke, p. 36. GUIDE CONTENT — TTW reference notes summarising the guide's assessment; the judgement is the guide's.*

The guide reads Sumrall's rise as increasingly typical of the modern game and traces it in full: four playing years at Kentucky, a graduate assistantship there in 2005-06, an FCS job at San Diego in his mid-20s, then up the ranks to co-defensive coordinator at Kentucky, two seasons as head coach at Troy and two at Tulane. It notes immediate success adds commas to a bank account in college football, with a CFP appearance in 2024 and at least 11 wins in three of four seasons. Its analytical point is about inheritance — a mess at Troy, a strong foundation at Tulane — and it places Florida somewhere in between.
